newsitem.title: UK: PIA ponders UK cargo charter extension.
newsitem.headline: PIA ponders UK cargo charter extension.

text.p: Pakistan International Airlines said it is considering extending a Karachi-London Heathrow Boeing 707F charter flight programme that began in early June and is scheduled to finish at end-September.

"This is under discussion now and I think it will be extended," the carrier's UK cargo marketing spokesman Nasim Rahimtoola told Reuters in a telephone interview, although he could not estimate by how long.
"The 707 is hushkitted and so we have received no objections, nor anticipate any, from the British authorities," he said.

He added that the temporary series of three weekly 707 freighter flights was the first PIA had operated between Pakistan and Britain -- freight had previously been carried on charters to Frankfurt and Paris and trucked on to London.
Rahimtoola said that an average of 35 tonnes was being carried on each cargo charter, with shipments ex-Pakistan to the UK comprising mainly fresh fruit and vegetables along with some textiles.
In the return direction, primarily machinery, pharmaceuticals and chemicals are being transported, he stated.

"Although rates are slightly down on those charged for our scheduled flights on the route, the programme has gone well. The average load factor from Pakistan is 90-85 percent and from London it is 75-80 percent," said Rahimtoola.
PIA also operates six weekly Boeing 747-200 scheduled flights a week between Heathrow and Karachi, one of which is flown by a Combi aircraft, and three weekly Manchester-Karachi 747-200 services.
Rahimtoola said that apart from similar consignments carried on the charters, freight on PIA's ex-UK scheduled flights also included vehicles and live animals.
Ex-London scheduled flights continue on to either Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta, or to Colombo and Mahe (Maldives).
Cargo space on regular flights operated by PIA from Karachi to Kathmandu, Dakha, Rangoon, Singapore, Tokyo, Riyadh and Dhahran is sold in the UK.
"The UK-Pakistan airfreight market is currently buoyant," noted Rahimtoola.
"Although the (strength of sterling) has had a slight impact on our export traffic from the UK, the present Pakistan government's import policies are beneficial to the growth of air cargo," he said.

Rahimtoola felt that an across-the-board rate ex-UK rate increase this autumn/winter was unlikely, although there could be rises introduced applicable to certain, but undisclosed, weight bands and to loose cargo.
